title: Cooperative clock-fencing and slice consolidation for cross-slice attention fallback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Investigate and implement a cooperative clock-fencing strategy combined with slice consolidation heuristics to improve end-to-end latency and throughput for attention-heavy workloads across H100, L40S, and A10 hosts when running MIG-partitioned instances. This ticket covers: (1) kernel selection signals for attention microkernels, (2) prefill/decode schedule adjustments to reduce cross-slice NVLink traffic, and (3) a conservative clock-steering policy that cooperates with MIG isolation and thermal constraints.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New kernel selector emits stable choices for >95% of observed token length distributions in our staging workloads; 2) End-to-end median tail latency (p95) for the attention-heavy eval suite reduces by >=12% on H100 MIG partitions compared to baseline; 3) No regressions (>2%) in throughput for mixed-latency workloads on L40S/A10; 4) Clock-fencing policy has telemetry and a kill-switch in console and passes safety review (QA runbook).
notes: This work must be safe to roll out to Dedicated pools. Primary risk is violating MIG isolation guarantees by aggressive cross-slice consolidation or clock boosts; hence the strategy is conservative and observable. We'll coordinate with infra ops for hardware stress testing windows.
decisions: 1) Use a hybrid kernel-selection heuristic: prefer int8/quant kernels for tokens-per-request > 512 and stable KV cache ratios; prefer fp16 microkernels for short-latency single-token decode scenarios. 2) Implement 'cross-slice coalescing' only when tenant affinity and MIG topology indicate low cross-slice NVLink hop counts. 3) Clock changes limited to +5% sustained across a partition and gated by thermal/clock headroom telemetry.
timeline: 2025-01-12: kickoff; 2025-01-20: prototype kernel selector and perf harness on H100-MIG; 2025-01-30: short-run stress tests and telemetry dashboards; 2025-02-04: CL for prefill scheduler; 2025-02-12: QA validation; 2025-02-18: staged rollout to dedicated pool 1.
hardware_test_notes: Used H100-40GB MIG 2g.20c and 1g.10c topologies; L40S runs on 48GB partitions; A10 runs on native single-GPU nodes for baseline comparison.
